 Boyce woman convicted in $17 million tax refund scheme 
 Jury returns guilty verdicts on all counts after about 40 minutes of deliberation 
 By KALB Digital Team Published : Nov. 19, 2026 at 12:04 PM CST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google ALEXANDRIA, La. (KALB) - A federal jury on Nov. 17 convicted Jane Frances Pierce, 64, of Boyce, of mail fraud, filing false tax returns, corruptly interfering with an IRS investigation and money laundering.
 RELATED: Boyce woman indicted for mail and tax fraud, corrupt interference and money laundering 
 After deliberating for approximately 40 minutes, the jury returned guilty verdicts on all counts. The court ordered Pierce to be held in custody pending sentencing.
 Evidence presented at trial
 According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Pierce filed false tax returns on behalf of a purported trust she controlled. The returns fraudulently claimed a total of almost $10 million in refunds.
 Pierce obtained more than $1 million from the IRS and used the funds for personal expenses, including purchasing a house and paying her relatives’ mortgages.
 When the IRS attempted to recover the refunds, Pierce obstructed the agency’s efforts by filing a false amended tax return, mailing the IRS a fake check, filing a false court document and laundering the remaining profits.
 Separately, Pierce filed a false tax return on behalf of a purported estate she controlled. The return claimed more than $7 million in refunds.
 Sentencing
 Pierce is scheduled to be sentenced Feb. 16. She faces maximum penalties of 20 years in federal prison for mail fraud, 10 years in prison for each money laundering charge and three years in prison for the false tax return and corrupt interference charges.
 Pierce also faces a period of supervised release, restitution and monetary penalties. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors.
 Officials’ statements
 “Jane Pierce filed false tax returns through a purported trust she controlled and used those filings to fraudulently claim nearly $10 million in refunds from the IRS,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “After obtaining more than $1 million in taxpayer funds, Pierce used the money for personal expenses and then tried to obstruct the IRS’s recovery efforts through additional false filings, a fake check, and money laundering. Today’s conviction makes clear that the Fraud Division will hold accountable those who steal from the American people and attempt to hide or obstruct their crimes.”
 “Tax fraudsters steal not just from the United States government but also from every person who works hard, pays their taxes, and trusts that everyone else is doing the same,” said U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller. “When that trust is undermined through theft by people like Ms. Pierce, citizens lose trust in the systems that serve and protect our communities and that they pay for with their hard-earned tax dollars. The people of Western Louisiana deserve honesty and accountability, and we will continue working with our law enforcement partners to hold those offenders accountable for their actions.”
 “This conviction sends a powerful message to those who believe they can exploit our nation’s tax system for personal financial gain,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Maisha Horton of IRS Criminal Investigation’s Atlanta Field Office. “IRS Criminal Investigation will investigate, uncover your schemes, and hold you accountable. I commend the outstanding work and unwavering determination of our IRS-CI special agents, whose investigative efforts were instrumental in securing this conviction, and thank the U.S. Attorney’s Office for its vigorous prosecution of this case. Together, we are sending an unmistakable message that stealing from the American taxpayer will have serious consequences.”
